To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a mitogen‐activated kinase‐like activity is detected in the pulvinus of tipped maize plants, and this kinase activity is important for the bending process; 2) the kinase activity is detected in a pattern that roughly corresponds to the time required for maize to become committed to bending; 3) treatment with an inhibitor of mitogen‐activated kinases reduces the bending response and the kinase activity; 4) the inhibitor can be rinsed out of the system, and
the maize pulvinous system can be used as a model for the study of MAPK activity and that MAPKs are important for the regulation of the maize pulvinar bending response.
MAPK activity in maize pulvini is differentially regulated in response to gravitropic stimulation, and that this activity is important for the bending of the pulvinar tissue.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the signalling events that occur in the maize gravitropic response.
understanding the signalling events that take place in the pulvinus of maize, and how these events are involved in the regulation of differential growth in response gravistimulation.
understanding the signalling events that occur in response to graviperception in the pulvinus and the role of MAPK in these events. © 1999 The Author.
